title: Check yourself: Keeping claims tied to their sources: summaries, conflicts and dates

questions.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. A consultancy report gives a market's growth for 2024 as 12%, and an equally reputable trade survey gives 9% for the same year. How should the final report treat the two?

options.text: Present both values with the name of each source and a note that they disagree
options.says: The guide's answer is "annotating conflicts with source attribution rather than arbitrarily selecting one value", so both values stay, each with its sources.

options.text: Present the value from the larger of the two publishers, because it is likelier to be right
options.says: Ruled out because "choosing one value hides a disagreement the reader needs".

options.text: Present a single figure between the two, which fairly reflects both of the sources
options.says: Ruled out because the averaged number "appears in no source and cannot be checked".

options.text: Present only the more recently published value and leave the other out for brevity
options.says: Ruled out because an agent that picks the newer figure "has made a decision that nobody asked it to make and that the reader cannot see".

origin.section: Keeping claims tied to their sources: summaries, conflicts and dates

questions.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. A report calls two numbers contradictory: one subagent found 7% in a source and another found 9% in a different source. Which change to the subagents' output prevents the misreading?

options.text: Require each subagent to rank its sources by how well known they are
options.says: Ruled out because ranking sources by reputation says nothing about when a number was gathered, and the page's rule turns on whether "Two findings for a claim with different values and the same date" exist.

options.text: Require a longer excerpt from each source around every number
options.says: Ruled out because an excerpt shows the wording and not the moment, and "Without dates, an agent cannot tell".

options.text: Require a publication or data collection date next to every value
options.says: The guide asks for dates "to prevent temporal differences from being misinterpreted as contradictions", since the date shows whether the two numbers describe the same moment.

options.text: Require the subagents to agree a single number before they return
options.says: Ruled out because "choosing one value hides a disagreement the reader needs".
